chunks: When he was old enough to go about with him, he said: "O my son, I dreamt that I was sacrificing you. Consider, what you think?" He replied: "Father, do as you are commanded. If God pleases you will find me firm."

key_terms.السَّعْيَ: the ability to walk or move about

ai.seo_question: What did Ibrahim say to his son regarding his dream of sacrifice?
ai.summary: In Surah As-Saffat, this pivotal dialogue highlights the mutual submission of Ibrahim and Ismail to divine will, with Ismail’s response 'Insha'Allah' underscoring the Shia emphasis on active patience (Sabr) rather than passive endurance. This event is traditionally linked to the sacrifice of Ismail, forming a core narrative for the Eid al-Adha and illustrating the perfection of prophetic obedience. The exchange serves as a model for believers to maintain steadfastness when tested by God's commands.
